items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: And the next Sunday, we had Willie Smith, Johnny Hodges, and 2 other alto players.

ctx.x: So we worked at the Trouville for awhile, and -- that was a real good job. We didn't go to work until 10 o'clock at night. We played at 10, and we -- you know, off at 10:30 and go back at 11, you know, go back on at 12, go back on at 1, and stay until 1:30, and that was the end of our gig.

But now the Trouville was where they had the best sessions - jam sessions - they ever had in Los Angeles. What we used to do at the Trouville -- the rhythm section was always Nat; you know, the trio and myself, most of the time. That was then, like, one Sunday, we had Lester, Ben, Bumps, and I don't know whether it was Don Bias or whoever, but we had the 4 tenor players. And the next Sunday, we had Willie Smith, Johnny Hodges, and 2 other alto players. And then

we had -- we'd always have the rhythm section but there would be a trumpet there; they would have Lloyd Reese, Rex Stewart, and Red Mack, who was a real good trumpet player here in town; Red Mack -- and someone else.
